title: overnight-fleet-congestion-slice-2026-11-02
content:
Overnight fleet congestion snapshot — data export for postmortem

Context:
- Incident window: 2026-11-01 22:30 UTC -> 2026-11-02 03:45 UTC. Reported symptoms: elevated p95/p99 token latency across hosted-api in eu-west and us-central, increased throttle events and queueing observed.
- This sheet is a consolidated extract used for RCA and capacity planning follow-ups. Pull combines telemetry (gpu/cpu/util, queue depth), scheduler events (preempt, migrate), and rate limiter/throttle logs.

Raw rows (one-line CSV-format for quick import):
timestamp,region,zone,instance_type,gpu_count,avg_gpu_util_pct,avg_cpu_util_pct,queue_depth_avg,queue_depth_peak,throttle_count,throttle_reasons,backpressure_ms,active_jobs_sample,dominant_model,p95_latency_ms,p99_latency_ms,error_rate_pct

2026-11-02T02:30:00Z,eu-west,eu-west-1a,n1-highgpu-8,8,93,71,18,56,104,rate-limit(65%),queueing(35%),960,74,redwood-13b,320,820,1.7

Aggregates (incident window):
- Regions impacted (by throttle_count > 20): eu-west, us-central. Minor impact in ap-southeast.
- Median GPU util (samples): 89%  | Median queue_depth_avg: 10 | Total throttle events observed: 293 in window
- Peak per-node backpressure: 960 ms observed on eu-west-1a at 2026-11-02T02:30Z
- Model mix during peaks: heavy fraction of redwood-13b (background batch reranks + low-latency chat requests) correlated with highest p99 latencies.

Quick hypotheses (for triage):
1) Cross-regional traffic spike + simultaneous model rollout increased seq length and KV cache misses for redwood-13b leading to longer decode times and pipeline queueing.
2) Autoscaler lag: burst of short-lived jobs saturated small-instance pools (2/4 GPU shapes) causing cascade of queueing onto 8-GPU machines.
3) Rate limiter policy mismatch: token-based quotas were being applied but spike was request-bursty (many short requests) causing token-bucket refills to produce transient high throttle counts rather than smoothing.

Queries used for extract (simplified):
- Telemetry join: SELECT ts, region, zone, instance_type, gpu_count, avg_gpu_util AS avg_gpu_util_pct, avg_cpu_util AS avg_cpu_util_pct, avg(queue_depth) AS queue_depth_avg, max(queue_depth) AS queue_depth_peak, sum(throttle_event) AS throttle_count, any_value(throttle_reason) AS throttle_reasons, avg(backpressure_ms) AS backpressure_ms FROM telemetry.node_1s WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-11-01T22:30:00Z' AND '2026-11-02T03:45:00Z' GROUP BY ts, region, zone, instance_type, gpu_count
- Workload join: SELECT job_id, model_family, request_type, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_p95, latency_p99 FROM workloads.jobs WHERE ts BETWEEN ... AND job_id IN (sample_active_jobs)

Notable observations and evidence:
- Evidence A: eu-west-1a repeated high backpressure spikes coincident with background batch rerank jobs starting a scheduled job at 02:15 UTC (see INFRA-8421). Batch job configuration used large-seq = true which disabled prefix KV caching for those requests.
- Evidence B: Autoscaler logs show scale-up events with 90s median provisioning time; scale decisions were conservative because node provisioning budget stepups capped at +10% per 15m window (see INFRA-8433).
- Evidence C: Rate limiter telemetry shows token refill rate configured for steady-state throughput; a burst of short requests (many under 50 tokens) created request-level contention not handled by token refill smoothing.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident (notes from Slack channel #infra-incident):
- Emergency canary rollback of the scheduled batch rerank in eu-west at 02:40 UTC. Reduced incoming long-seq background work by ~60% in 12 minutes.
- Temporary increase in per-region soft autoscaler budget for us-central and eu-west to allow faster scale-ups (applied 02:55 UTC).
- Short-term rate limiter tweak: switched request-count smoothing window from 60s -> 10s for hosted-api ingress to reduce burst amplification (03:10 UTC).

Follow-ups / action items: (owners assigned)
- Fix: add KV-cache-aware job annotation so scheduler can separate long-seq batch reranks from low-latency chat workloads. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-11-10.
- Fix: review autoscaler budget step and reduce provisioning cap during business hours; add predictive headroom for scheduled batch jobs. Owner: Jonah Alvarez. Due: 2026-11-17.
- Investigate: rate limiter policy redesign for mixed request-size traffic patterns (token vs request smoothing hybrid). Owner: Riley Chen. Due: 2026-11-24.

Appendix: snippets from logs (redacted) and sample chart notes:
- eu-west-1a backpressure timeline: 22:40->23:30 low, 23:30->00:00 ramp, 02:15->02:45 max spike (aligned with batch start), post-rollback drop 02:55->03:15.
- Suggest adding a dedicated capacity pool for scheduled batch reranks (4 x 8-GPU reserved for nightly windows) to avoid consumer-visible interference.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Need to verify whether preemption events caused additional cache invalidation and exacerbated seq-decode timeouts.
- Should run a synthetic workload (mixed short chat + long-seq batch) against a staging autoscaler config to reproduce scale lag.

References: JIRA INFRA-8421 (batch rerank rollout), JIRA INFRA-8433 (autoscaler budget), Slack #infra-incident thread (link redacted), GH PR runtimes#918 (rate limiter change)

End of export.
